subject.title: fix: gateway restart no longer takes the service down into a known-fatal auth migration

question: After real lifecycle proof is supplied, should the protected gateway/auth owners accept this preflight as the canonical safeguard for migration-required restarts?
rationale: The change intentionally alters the order of an operationally sensitive gateway lifecycle path; maintainer intent is needed to accept that user-visible service-management contract.

options.title: Accept after live proof
options.body: Verify that a managed gateway remains running when restart is blocked, then merge the bounded preflight change.

options.title: Request a different lifecycle policy
options.body: Keep the runtime migration refusal and specify a different owner-approved recovery flow if preflight blocking is not the desired operator contract.

recommendation.title: Accept after live proof
recommendation.body: Verify that a managed gateway remains running when restart is blocked, then merge the bounded preflight change.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied context identifies this person as the author of the proposed lifecycle/auth boundary change; stronger current-main ownership evidence was unavailable.
